blocks: The fifth button down the right-hand column opens Probability view. Select a step in the top half of the grid, then press a pad on the eight-pad slider at the top of the Play Area to set the chance that its notes play, from 13% to 100%.

The sixth button down the right-hand column opens Mutation view. Select a step in the top half of the grid, then press a pad on the eight-pad slider at the top of the Play Area to vary the pitch of its notes during playback. The leftmost pad means no Mutation.

The seventh button down the right-hand column opens Micro Step editing view. Select a step in the top half of the grid; the six leftmost pads of the Play Area's top row are that step's Micro Steps, for finer note placement within the step.
The eighth button down the right-hand column. It is an action rather than a view: it transfers the selected track's current Pattern or Pattern chain into an Ableton Live clip slot.
Works only while connected to Ableton Live.
Hold Shift and press Sequencer to open Sequencer Settings, which controls each track's type and MIDI channel, plus the scale and root note.
Hold Shift and press Stop Clip to open Swing view, shown in orange and white. A value above 50 delays off-beat notes and a value below 50 moves them earlier; the Up and Down arrows adjust it.
Hold Shift and press Device to open Tempo view, shown in blue and white. The number is the current BPM; the Up and Down arrows adjust it.

Statement: a method may call methods only on itself, its parameters, objects it creates, and its own direct component objects — never reach through one object to act on something that object merely holds. Law of Demeter (General Formulation): "Only talk to your immediate friends" / "Each unit should only talk to its friends; Don't talk to strangers."

Origin: discovered at Northeastern University in the fall of 19/8/7 by Person/Ian Holland, while working on the Demeter Project; first published in Lieberherr & Holland, "Object-Oriented Programming: An Objective Sense of Style," OOPSLA '88. Law of Demeter: Principle of Least Knowledge (Karl Lieberherr's own page): "The name 'Law of Demeter' was chosen because the style rule was discovered while working on The Demeter Project ... (Demeter = Greek Goddess of Agriculture; grow software in small steps.)"

Kind: heuristic — a specific case of the general Low Coupling Principle, adopted as a style rule rather than proved as a theorem. Law of Demeter (General Formulation): "In this general form, the LoD is a more specific case of the Low Coupling Principle well-known in software engineering."

Example: flagged in My/Pref/Dev/Tool/Secrets/fnox against the 1Password CLI, whose finest-grained access boundary is the Vault — any script that needs one secret ends up holding standing access to every secret in that Vault, the law's warning made concrete.
Epistemics/Concept/Heuristic vs Axiom — why this is a heuristic, not the Logseq/Entity/Axiom-grade natural law a literal reading of "law" might suggest.
